newsitem.title: USA: N.J. candidate blasts Whitman's pension bond plan.
newsitem.headline: N.J. candidate blasts Whitman's pension bond plan.

text.p: U.S. Rep. Rob Andrews, D-N.J., kicked off his campaign for governor with a swing across New Jersey in which he blasted Gov. Christine Whitman's $2.9 billion pension bond plan.
Andrews told elementary school students in Union City they would still be paying off the debt when they turned 50.

Whitman has proposed selling the bonds to pay off the pension system's unfunded liability. But opposition to the deal is mounting in the Legislature, and it has become an issue in the November election.

A poll released Thursday by Quinnipiac College showed a drop in Whitman's approval rating, in part because of skepticism about the bond proposal. About 49 percent of those surveyed called the idea "a gimmick to balance the state budget," while 19 percent said it is "good financial management."
The state in February selected Merrill Lynch & Co to underwrite the bonds.

Andrews is the second Democratic candidate this week to make his official announcement entering the race, joining state Sen. Jim McGreevey. Former Morris County Prosecutor Michael Murphy is expected to join the race by end of the week.
Despite Whitman's declining approval rating, the Quinnipiac poll found she would handily beat any of the three candidates if the election were held now.
The poll surveyed 867 New Jersey residents who said they were registered voters. It was conducted April 1 through 6, and has a margin of error of plus or minus 3.3 percent.
